description: What SHOW PROCEDURES reports after a CREATE PROCEDURE. The rows are SCANNED rather than read positionally, because both backends list the whole built-in library alongside the user-defined procedures, so the one just created is not necessarily the first row. A simple procedure, one with no parameters, a SCHEMA-QUALIFIED one (listed once that schema is in use), one with several parameters, one carrying an IF (which is also CALLed, to show the body is a well-formed scripting block and not merely stored text), and one with a WHILE loop and an OBJECT return are each found by name. DROP PROCEDURE removes it - counted by the user-defined rows, is_builtin = 'N', so the built-ins are not in the way - and DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS on the now-missing name does not throw. Creating two leaves two user-defined rows. The bodies here reference tables that mostly do not exist, which is deliberate: CREATE PROCEDURE stores the body without resolving it. This is the listing-side companion of scripting-create-procedure, which CALLs each procedure and checks its effects. Converted 1:1 from scripting/CreateProcedureJdbcTest (now retired); the Java scanned the SHOW PROCEDURES ResultSet row by row through JDBC, which becomes a RESULT_SCAN over the same SHOW.

steps.sql: CREATE PROCEDURE update_data(id INTEGER, value VARCHAR) RETURNS VARCHAR AS 'BEGIN UPDATE data_rows SET label = :value WHERE id = :id; RETURN ''updated''; END'
CREATE PROCEDURE cleanup() RETURNS VARCHAR AS 'BEGIN DELETE FROM temp_table; RETURN ''cleaned''; END'
CREATE PROCEDURE my_schema.process_orders(order_id INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER AS 'BEGIN RETURN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders); END'
CREATE PROCEDURE insert_record(name VARCHAR, age INTEGER, active BOOLEAN) RETURNS INTEGER AS 'BEGIN INSERT INTO people (name, age, active) VALUES (:name, :age, :active); RETURN 1; END'
CREATE PROCEDURE test_proc(x INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER AS 'BEGIN RETURN x * 2; END'
CREATE PROCEDURE proc1(x INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER AS 'BEGIN RETURN x; END'
CREATE PROCEDURE proc2(x INTEGER, y INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER AS 'BEGIN RETURN x + y; END'
CREATE TABLE test_table (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
CREATE PROCEDURE check_value(max_count INTEGER) RETURNS VARCHAR AS 'DECLARE outcome VARCHAR; BEGIN IF (max_count > 2) THEN outcome := ''many''; ELSE outcome := ''few''; END IF; RETURN outcome; END'

CREATE PROCEDURE process_with_loop(max_iterations INTEGER) RETURNS OBJECT AS 'DECLARE counter INTEGER := 0; outcome OBJECT; BEGIN WHILE (counter < 10) DO counter := counter + 1; END WHILE; outcome := OBJECT_CONSTRUCT(''count'', counter, ''status'', ''completed''); RETURN outcome; END'
